facts.label: Version and basis relationships
facts.text: 1. Adjusted EBITDA definition. S4 page:27 states "During the first quarter of 2026, the Company changed its definition of Adjusted EBITDA to adjust for net periodic pension cost." and "All comparative period information for Adjusted EBITDA has been re-cast to conform with the current definition." The recast covers the 2025 interim periods shown in S4. S1 page:77 reports FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA under the earlier definition and no recast FY2025 figure was located in the supplied set. S7 page:11 repeats the change. Consequence: a trailing twelve-month figure that adds FY2025, nine months of 2026 and nine months of 2025 spans two definitions; the size of the effect on FY2025 is not supplied. 2. Debt table versions. The December 31, 2025 table (S1 page:142), the March 31 and June 30, 2026 tables (S2 page:11-12, S3 page:11-12) and the September 30, 2026 table (S4 page:12) are successive dated views, not duplicates; each controls only its own date. S3 page:12 notes in footnote 1 that the 2026 line "Includes $125.5 million for the 6.125% Senior Subordinated Notes due 2027", which S4 page:45 reports as redeemed on July 24, 2026. 3. Post-quarter structure. S4 page:38 prints a second maturity table "after giving effect to the 2026 Refinancing Transactions". It is a pro forma view beside the September 30, 2026 table, not a replacement for it. 4. Instrument aliases inside the debt note. The September 30, 2026 table lists "Credit Agreement-Term Loans due 2029", while S4 page:84 refers to "we repaid all of the outstanding Muvico Term Loans". S3 page:68 defines the Muvico Term Loans as the new term loans maturing in 2029 under the Muvico Credit Agreement, so the two names refer to one facility on the filings' own wording. The same filings call the notes issued by Muvico "New 2029 Notes" in text and "Senior Secured Notes due 2029" in the table, and the "Existing 7.5% Notes" appear in the table as "7.5% First Lien Notes due 2029". Downstream modules must keep one name per instrument and cite both. 5. Entity roles. Holdings is the registrant and, in the 2026 refinancing, the borrower of the new first and second lien term loans and issuer of the new notes (S4 page:33-34). Muvico, LLC and Centertainment Development, LLC form the Muvico Group, described in S3 page:67 as "are unrestricted subsidiaries under the indenture governing Holdings". Odeon Finco is an indirect subsidiary that borrowed the Odeon term loans and was guaranteed by Holdings "on a standalone and unsecured basis" (S2 page:27). After October 5, 2026 the collateral groups are described as the AMC Collateral, the Centertainment Collateral and the Odeon group (S4 page:37). 6. Authority order. Filed statements and notes (S1 to S4) control facts; releases (S5 to S7) are attributed management claims. No conflict between a release and a filing was found in the locators checked. The one claim with no filing counterpart is the "approximately 97%" refinancing share in S7 page:4.

- Subsequent-event financial effect: S4 page:38 "The Company estimates that it will record a loss on extinguishment of approximately $182.7 million".

- Liquidity statement: S4 page:6 "The Company believes its existing cash and cash equivalents, together with cash generated from operations, will be sufficient to fund its operations and satisfy its obligations currently and through the next twelve months." Cash and restricted cash are separate balance-sheet lines (S4 page:3) and restricted cash is described as cash held as landlord guarantees and cash-collateralized letters of credit (S4 page:7).

- Facilities: a keyword search of all seven sources for "revolv", "undrawn", "credit facility", "borrowing base", "availability under" and "letters of credit" found only the 2013 revolving facility, described in the past tense with a stated maturity of April 22, 2024 (S1 page:161: "maturing April 22, 2024") and the restricted-cash letters of credit. No current revolving or other committed undrawn facility is described.

- Covenants: each reporting date carries a compliance statement, for example S4 page:17 "the Company believes that it was in full compliance with all agreements, including related covenants, governing its outstanding debt." and S1 page:165 for December 31, 2025. The covenant summaries in the notes describe restrictions on debt, liens, restricted payments, investments, asset sales, mergers and affiliate transactions (S4 page:35-36). A keyword search of all seven sources for "financial covenant", "coverage ratio", "springing" and "minimum liquidity" found nothing; "fixed charge" appears only as English-law security over Odeon assets (S2 page:28). The only leverage test found is the Total Leverage Ratio that set the interest rate on the New 2029 Notes (S1 page:146 and S4 page:84), which were redeemed on October 5, 2026 (S4 page:38).

facts.text: AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. enters the cutoff with sharply better reported earnings, a refinanced and longer-dated but larger debt stack, and cash as its only stated source of liquidity. Adjusted EBITDA for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 is 840.4, built from FY2025 (387.5), nine months of 2026 (707.2) less nine months of 2025 (254.3); against principal debt of 3,782.6 that is 4.50x, and 3.61x net of unrestricted cash of 751.9, down from 10.39x and 9.28x at FY2025. Cash interest paid over the same twelve months was 392.3, so Adjusted EBITDA covered it 2.14x, against 0.95x in FY2025. Free cash flow turned positive on the trailing basis at 168.0 after a deficit of 365.9 in FY2025. Most of the improvement comes from the earnings side: principal fell from 4,024.2 to 3,782.6 while Adjusted EBITDA rose from 387.5 to 840.4. These ratios are the clearest evidence of recovery and rest on filed statements, but they carry three qualifications. First, the trailing figure mixes the pre-2026 and the 2026 Adjusted EBITDA definitions (the effect on FY2025 is not supplied). Second, the 2026 operating cash flow is seasonal: the first quarter used 128.5, the second quarter provided 235.4 and the third 176.6. Third, no revolving or other committed undrawn facility is described anywhere in the sources, so liquidity is cash of 751.9 and no more; the working capital deficit excluding restricted cash was still 792.8. On October 5, 2026, after the quarter end, the company issued 2,000.0 of 8.875% first lien notes due 2031, borrowed 850.0 of first lien term loans due 2031 and 1,120.0 of 11.25% second lien term loans due 2033, and repaid or discharged the Muvico and Odeon term loans, the New 2029 Notes and the Existing 7.5% Notes. Pro forma principal is 4,086.1 (4.86x on trailing Adjusted EBITDA); before 2030 only 8.5 a year of first lien term loan amortization falls due, and 79.2% of principal is fixed rate. The stated coupons on the two new fixed-rate instruments alone come to 303.5 a year, and the floating margin on the first lien term loan is not printed, so pro forma interest cover cannot be computed from the sources. Operating lease liabilities of 3,761.9 and the 454.3 exhibitor services agreement liability sit outside the debt figure and are fixed claims on the same cash flow. Covenant headroom cannot be assessed: the filings give compliance statements but no covenant levels.

Total interest expense includes non-cash interest on the exhibitor services agreement (55.2 in 9M 2026) and PIK interest (46.7 add-back in the cash flow), so cash interest paid is the cover denominator.

- Covenant levels and headroom: Not supplied. No maintenance covenant level appears in the filings; executed debt documents are not supplied.

- Quarterly data for 2025: only the Q3 2025 and nine-month 2025 comparatives are printed in the 2026 reports; a discrete Q4 2025 quarter is not printed and would be FY2025 less 9M 2025 on mixed definitions.
- Cash held abroad: the split of 751.9 between U.S. markets (606.3) and International markets (145.6) is printed (S4 page:7), but transfer restrictions are not assessed.
- Group-level view: the Q3 2026 report has no Muvico Group or restricted-group presentation; the last such view is in the June 30, 2026 report (S3 page:67-73) and is not used here.
- Fiscal-year-end 2026 balance sheet and the effect of the refinancing on interest expense are after the cutoff and not in the sources.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. is a listed, widely held theatre circuit with no sponsor identified in the supplied sources, and its creditor story is the interaction of an operating recovery with a history of active balance-sheet engineering. The operating base is large and geographically split: 855 theatres and 9,640 screens in 11 countries at December 31, 2025, and 840 theatres and 9,472 screens at September 30, 2026, with U.S. markets contributing 3,298.5 of 4,353.2 of nine-month 2026 revenue. Revenue is driven by attendance, which depends on a film slate controlled by a few studios, so revenue visibility is short and cash flow is seasonal. Against that, a largely fixed cost base (rent, operating expense and leases) gave strong operating leverage in 2026: third quarter revenue rose 31.6% and Adjusted EBITDA margin was 20.3% against 9.4%. The credit-relevant history is a sequence of transactions that moved debt and assets between entities: the July 2024 transfer of 175 theatres and intellectual property to unrestricted subsidiaries, the July 2025 exchange of part of the Existing 7.5% Notes into Muvico notes, repeated exchanges of debt for shares, and the October 5, 2026 refinancing that repaid the Muvico and Odeon term loans, the New 2029 Notes and most of the Existing 7.5% Notes with 2,000.0 of first lien notes, 850.0 of first lien term loans and 1,120.0 of second lien term loans. That refinancing is a subsequent event to the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and is kept separate from period facts below. Supportive actions are also documented, namely large equity issuance and note-for-share exchanges, but they were dilutive: shares outstanding rose from 512,943,561 at December 31, 2025 to 892,604,638 at September 30, 2026. Ownership concentration, sponsor behaviour beyond the issuer's own actions, and executed covenant terms cannot be read from the sources and remain open.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The transaction that matters most for creditors is the October 5, 2026 refinancing, which closed after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and is a subsequent event. S4 page:33 states that on that date "the Company completed a series of refinancing transactions", issuing 2,000.0 of 8.875% First Lien Notes due 2031 as issuer, borrowing 850.0 of first lien term loans under an amended and restated credit agreement, and borrowing 1,120.0 of second lien term loans from a lender identified as Deutsche Bank Special Situations Group (S4 page:34). The first lien term loans mature on October 5, 2031 with 0.25% quarterly amortization from March 31, 2027, and the second lien term loans mature on October 5, 2033 at a fixed 11.25% (S4 page:36). The 2031 Notes are secured on a first-priority basis, pari passu with the first lien term loans, by substantially all tangible and intangible assets of the company and the guarantors (S4 page:35). Intercreditor agreements separate three collateral groups: the AMC collateral, the Centertainment group and the Odeon group, and rank the Existing Exchangeable Notes first lien on the AMC collateral but second lien on the Centertainment collateral (S4 page:37). The proceeds repaid in full the Muvico Term Loans and the Odeon Term Loans, redeemed all 903.4 of the New 2029 Notes at 100.000% plus a make-whole premium of 144.3, accepted tenders for 355.5 of the 360.0 Existing 7.5% Notes and discharged the remainder for redemption on or about February 15, 2027 (S4 page:37-38). The company used about 32.7 of balance-sheet cash at closing and estimates a loss on extinguishment of about 182.7 in the fourth quarter of 2026 (S4 page:38). Taken from the CP-1 accepted figures, pro forma principal is 4,086.1 against 3,782.6 before, with 79.2% fixed rate, and the nearest large maturity moves from 2029 to 2031. The creditor mechanics are two: near-term refinancing risk falls, because the Muvico term loans, the Odeon term loans and the New 2029 Notes were the main 2029 and 2031 obligations; but senior secured claims are larger and a 1,120.0 second lien layer now sits behind 2,850.0 of new first lien debt, so recovery prospects for junior claims depend on collateral value that the sources do not quantify. This handoff states no expected recovery.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Earlier transactions explain why the structure is layered. On July 22, 2024 the company transferred the net assets of 175 theatres and 100% of certain intellectual property to Muvico through Centertainment, and Muvico licensed the intellectual property back to the operating subsidiary and engaged it under a management agreement to run the transferred theatres; Muvico and Centertainment (the Muvico Group) "are unrestricted subsidiaries under the indenture governing Holdings" for the purposes of the Existing 7.5% Notes (S1 page:100, S3 page:67). In the same month the company and Muvico jointly borrowed 2,024.3 of term loans and Muvico issued 414.4 of exchangeable notes to repurchase second lien notes (S1 page:156). In July 2025, under a transaction support agreement with "certain holders" of the Existing 7.5% Notes, Muvico issued 857.0 of New 2029 Notes for 590.0 of those notes plus 244.4 of new money (S1 page:95; S4 page:16), reducing the Existing 7.5% Notes from 950.0 at December 31, 2024 to 360.0 at December 31, 2025 (S1 page:142). The sources do not say whether every holder was offered the exchange. In 2026 the company paid consent fees in shares rather than cash, including 17,739,549 shares to holders of the New 2029 Notes for indenture amendments, exchanged all 155.8 of the New Exchangeable Notes for 142,102,295 shares with a loss on extinguishment of 33.0, refinanced the 400.0 Odeon Senior Secured Notes due 2027 with 425.0 of Odeon term loans that carried a Holdings guarantee, and raised equity (S4 page:14-18; S2 page:27). The 125.5 Senior Subordinated Notes due 2027 were redeemed on July 24, 2026 with proceeds of the June 2026 registered direct offering, within net equity issuance proceeds of 333.6 for nine months 2026 (S4 page:4, page:16, page:45). No dividends or shareholder distributions are printed in the nine-month cash flow statement (S4 page:4). Evidence quality for these transactions is High: they are filed, dated and issuer-specific, but executed indentures and credit agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity (what the documents permit) is inferred only from the filings' summaries.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. is a recovering but thinly cushioned credit: earnings have rebounded sharply, yet its fixed charges leave little margin if film attendance weakens. The strongest support is trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 840.4 million, which brings total debt to 4.50x, cash interest cover to 2.14x and free cash flow to USD 168.0 million, while cash of USD 751.9 million and the October 2026 refinancing push the main maturities to 2031 and 2033. The weakest point is that liquidity is cash alone, with no committed facility described, and fixed-charge cover including rent is only about 1.35x. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filings and releases are enough to support the financial, business, transaction, credit and evidence-trace work, with stated limitations. Nothing is blocked. | Medium | No executed debt documents are supplied, so covenant terms rest on filing summaries only. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Audited annual and three quarterly filings cover FY2025 and every quarter of 2026 to September 30, 2026. | Leverage, coverage and liquidity work can rest on filed statements, not management claims. | High |

| The October 5, 2026 refinancing is disclosed only as a subsequent event, after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet. | Balance sheet debt and the new structure are on different dates; users must keep them apart. | High |
| No committed undrawn facility is described in the current sources. | Liquidity analysis should rest on reported cash; no facility headroom can be assumed. | Medium |
| Adjusted EBITDA was redefined in 2026 and only 2025 interim periods were recast. | A twelve-month figure mixes definitions unless the effect is disclosed or adjusted. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The supplied set is ready with limitations for the minimum credit snapshot of AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. as of 2026-11-05, and no consumer is conditional or blocked. The set holds one audited annual report (FY2025), three unaudited quarterly reports (Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026) and three earnings releases that stand in for investor presentations, so every quarter of 2026 and the full prior year are covered by filed statements. The strongest evidence is the Q3 2026 quarterly report: it carries the September 30, 2026 balance sheet, nine-month cash flows, a debt note, segment Adjusted EBITDA reconciliations and a subsequent-events note on the October 5, 2026 refinancing, all inside the cutoff. The strongest contrary points are that the executed indentures and credit agreements are referenced but not supplied, that no committed undrawn facility is described anywhere in the set, that the Adjusted EBITDA definition changed in the first quarter of 2026, and that the Q3 2026 report drops the separate Muvico Group presentation that earlier reports carried. Each of these narrows what downstream modules may assert; none removes a source the owners need. The next evidence action is to add the Form 8-K exhibits that carry the new financing documents if covenant-level work is later selected. This view tests source sufficiency only (SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY); the model input contract was not evaluated (CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED).
### Source-by-source assessment

Identity of the reporting perimeter: every filing is made by AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. (called Holdings in the filings) on a consolidated basis. S4 page:5 states "The condensed consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Holdings and all subsidiaries" and S1 page:7 states "owns, operates or has interests in theatres located in the United States and Europe". Context lists no separate borrower, parent or guarantor, and the filings name none above Holdings. Reportable segments are U.S. markets and International markets (S4 page:5: "The Company manages its business under two reportable segments for its theatrical exhibition operations, U.S. markets and International markets.").

Debt table is as of December 31, 2025, before the 2026 exchanges and the October 5, 2026 refinancing |

Quarter figures are not annualizable by themselves |

Cross-checks made only to confirm that the releases point at the same filed facts, not to reconcile them: S7 page:9 prints "Corporate borrowings (principal amount)" in the same balance-sheet extract that S4 page:12 titles "Total principal amount of corporate borrowings", and S7 page:5 describes the footprint as "approximately 840 theatres and 9,500 screens across the globe".
### Version and basis relationships

1. Adjusted EBITDA definition. S4 page:27 states "During the first quarter of 2026, the Company changed its definition of Adjusted EBITDA to adjust for net periodic pension cost." and "All comparative period information for Adjusted EBITDA has been re-cast to conform with the current definition." The recast covers the 2025 interim periods shown in S4. S1 page:77 reports FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA under the earlier definition and no recast FY2025 figure was located in the supplied set. S7 page:11 repeats the change. Consequence: a trailing twelve-month figure that adds FY2025, nine months of 2026 and nine months of 2025 spans two definitions; the size of the effect on FY2025 is not supplied.

2. Debt table versions. The December 31, 2025 table (S1 page:142), the March 31 and June 30, 2026 tables (S2 page:11-12, S3 page:11-12) and the September 30, 2026 table (S4 page:12) are successive dated views, not duplicates; each controls only its own date. S3 page:12 notes in footnote 1 that the 2026 line "Includes $125.5 million for the 6.125% Senior Subordinated Notes due 2027", which S4 page:45 reports as redeemed on July 24, 2026.

3. Post-quarter structure. S4 page:38 prints a second maturity table "after giving effect to the 2026 Refinancing Transactions". It is a pro forma view beside the September 30, 2026 table, not a replacement for it.

4. Instrument aliases inside the debt note. The September 30, 2026 table lists "Credit Agreement-Term Loans due 2029", while S4 page:84 refers to "we repaid all of the outstanding Muvico Term Loans". S3 page:68 defines the Muvico Term Loans as the new term loans maturing in 2029 under the Muvico Credit Agreement, so the two names refer to one facility on the filings' own wording. The same filings call the notes issued by Muvico "New 2029 Notes" in text and "Senior Secured Notes due 2029" in the table, and the "Existing 7.5% Notes" appear in the table as "7.5% First Lien Notes due 2029". Downstream modules must keep one name per instrument and cite both.

5. Entity roles. Holdings is the registrant and, in the 2026 refinancing, the borrower of the new first and second lien term loans and issuer of the new notes (S4 page:33-34). Muvico, LLC and Centertainment Development, LLC form the Muvico Group, described in S3 page:67 as "are unrestricted subsidiaries under the indenture governing Holdings". Odeon Finco is an indirect subsidiary that borrowed the Odeon term loans and was guaranteed by Holdings "on a standalone and unsecured basis" (S2 page:27). After October 5, 2026 the collateral groups are described as the AMC Collateral, the Centertainment Collateral and the Odeon group (S4 page:37).

6. Authority order. Filed statements and notes (S1 to S4) control facts; releases (S5 to S7) are attributed management claims. No conflict between a release and a filing was found in the locators checked. The one claim with no filing counterpart is the "approximately 97%" refinancing share in S7 page:4.
### Debt, liquidity and covenant evidence located

- Debt detail: the Q3 2026 table lists each instrument with carrying and principal amounts (S4 page:12: "Total principal amount of corporate borrowings"), and the maturity schedule by year as of September 30, 2026 sits beside it on the same chunk. The refinancing terms in Note 11 give issuer, rate, maturity, security and guarantor language: for the new first lien notes S4 page:33 "The Company issued $2,000.0 million aggregate principal amount of 8.875% First Lien Notes due 2031"; for the new first lien term loans S4 page:36 "initial aggregate principal amount of $850.0 million, which mature on October 5, 2031"; for the new second lien term loans S4 page:34 "borrowed $1,120.0 million of new second lien term loans".
- Subsequent-event financial effect: S4 page:38 "The Company estimates that it will record a loss on extinguishment of approximately $182.7 million".

- Liquidity statement: S4 page:6 "The Company believes its existing cash and cash equivalents, together with cash generated from operations, will be sufficient to fund its operations and satisfy its obligations currently and through the next twelve months." Cash and restricted cash are separate balance-sheet lines (S4 page:3) and restricted cash is described as cash held as landlord guarantees and cash-collateralized letters of credit (S4 page:7).

- Facilities: a keyword search of all seven sources for "revolv", "undrawn", "credit facility", "borrowing base", "availability under" and "letters of credit" found only the 2013 revolving facility, described in the past tense with a stated maturity of April 22, 2024 (S1 page:161: "maturing April 22, 2024") and the restricted-cash letters of credit. No current revolving or other committed undrawn facility is described.

### Financial base view

AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. enters the cutoff with sharply better reported earnings, a refinanced and longer-dated but larger debt stack, and cash as its only stated source of liquidity. Adjusted EBITDA for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 is 840.4, built from FY2025 (387.5), nine months of 2026 (707.2) less nine months of 2025 (254.3); against principal debt of 3,782.6 that is 4.50x, and 3.61x net of unrestricted cash of 751.9, down from 10.39x and 9.28x at FY2025. Cash interest paid over the same twelve months was 392.3, so Adjusted EBITDA covered it 2.14x, against 0.95x in FY2025. Free cash flow turned positive on the trailing basis at 168.0 after a deficit of 365.9 in FY2025. Most of the improvement comes from the earnings side: principal fell from 4,024.2 to 3,782.6 while Adjusted EBITDA rose from 387.5 to 840.4. These ratios are the clearest evidence of recovery and rest on filed statements, but they carry three qualifications. First, the trailing figure mixes the pre-2026 and the 2026 Adjusted EBITDA definitions (the effect on FY2025 is not supplied). Second, the 2026 operating cash flow is seasonal: the first quarter used 128.5, the second quarter provided 235.4 and the third 176.6. Third, no revolving or other committed undrawn facility is described anywhere in the sources, so liquidity is cash of 751.9 and no more; the working capital deficit excluding restricted cash was still 792.8. On October 5, 2026, after the quarter end, the company issued 2,000.0 of 8.875% first lien notes due 2031, borrowed 850.0 of first lien term loans due 2031 and 1,120.0 of 11.25% second lien term loans due 2033, and repaid or discharged the Muvico and Odeon term loans, the New 2029 Notes and the Existing 7.5% Notes. Pro forma principal is 4,086.1 (4.86x on trailing Adjusted EBITDA); before 2030 only 8.5 a year of first lien term loan amortization falls due, and 79.2% of principal is fixed rate. The stated coupons on the two new fixed-rate instruments alone come to 303.5 a year, and the floating margin on the first lien term loan is not printed, so pro forma interest cover cannot be computed from the sources. Operating lease liabilities of 3,761.9 and the 454.3 exhibitor services agreement liability sit outside the debt figure and are fixed claims on the same cash flow. Covenant headroom cannot be assessed: the filings give compliance statements but no covenant levels.

No maintenance financial covenant, level or headroom is printed in any supplied source, so covenant metrics are Not supplied. The only ratio-linked terms found were the Total Leverage Ratio pricing grids on the Muvico Term Loans and the New 2029 Notes (S4 page:83, page:84), both repaid on October 5, 2026. The Adjusted EBITDA definition is described as "broadly consistent" with the definition in the debt indentures (S1 page:77), but the indenture definitions are not supplied.
### Definition and basis risks

1. Adjusted EBITDA definition. The company "changed its definition of Adjusted EBITDA to adjust for net periodic pension cost" in the first quarter of 2026 and recast 2025 comparatives, with an improvement of 0.3 for Q3 2025 and 0.9 for 9M 2025 (S4 page:27). FY2025 and FY2024 (S1 page:77) are not recast, so the LTM figure mixes definitions; the sensitivity in C1 is 0.9.
2. Total debt basis. Total debt here is principal, not carrying value, and excludes finance leases (shown separately) and all operating leases.
3. Cash basis. Net debt deducts unrestricted cash only. Cash of 145.6 of the 751.9 is held by the International markets operations (S4 page:7); access to it is not assessed here.

4. Balance sheet date versus structure. The September 30, 2026 balance sheet predates the October 5, 2026 refinancing; the pro forma rows use the printed post-refinancing principal and an estimate of cash used.

5. Interest. Total interest expense includes non-cash interest on the exhibitor services agreement (55.2 in 9M 2026) and PIK interest (46.7 add-back in the cash flow), so cash interest paid is the cover denominator.
## Calculations
All inputs are printed figures cited above, in USD millions. Results are rounded half-up to the shown places.
C1. Trailing twelve months to September 30, 2026 equals FY2025 plus 9M 2026 less 9M 2025.

- Adjusted EBITDA: 387.5 + 707.2 - 254.3 = 840.4. Sensitivity: if the 9M 2025 comparative were on the earlier definition (254.3 less the 0.9 improvement = 253.4), the LTM would be 387.5 + 707.2 - 253.4 = 841.3.
- Total interest expense: 530.2 + 405.9 - 388.0 = 548.1.
- Capital expenditures: 246.1 + 158.8 - 162.7 = 242.2.
C2. LTM cash interest paid: 406.9 + 270.9 - 285.5 = 392.3.
C3. Leverage. Total debt over Adjusted EBITDA, with principal as total debt.

C5. Free cash flow equals operating cash flow less capital expenditures: LTM 410.2 - 242.2 = 168.0; FY2025 (119.8) - 246.1 = (365.9); FY2024 (50.8) - 245.5 = (296.3); 9M 2026 283.5 - 158.8 = 124.7, equal to the printed 124.7 (S7 page:9); 9M 2025 (246.5) - 162.7 = (409.2), equal to the printed (409.2).

C7. Stated coupons on the two fixed-rate new instruments: 2,000.0 x 8.875% = 177.5 and 1,120.0 x 11.25% = 126.0, total 303.5 a year. This excludes the first lien term loan margin and the Existing Exchangeable Notes coupon, so it is a partial figure.
C9. Tie-outs, all equal to printed totals.
- Quarterly operating cash flow 2026: (128.5) + 235.4 + 176.6 = 283.5.

C10. Refinancing bridge using September 30 principal: repaid or discharged 1,979.2 + 423.9 + 903.4 + 360.0 = 3,666.5; raised 2,000.0 + 850.0 + 1,120.0 = 3,970.0; 3,782.6 - 3,666.5 = 116.1 stays; 116.1 + 3,970.0 = 4,086.1, equal to the printed total.

C11. Direction checks. Leverage fell from 10.39 (FY2025) to 4.50 (LTM): both calculated in C3. Cash rose from 428.5 at December 31, 2025 to 751.9 at September 30, 2026 (S1 page:114; S4 page:3). Principal fell from 4,024.2 to 3,782.6 (S1 page:142; S4 page:12).
## Gaps

- Undrawn committed facilities: Not supplied. No source describes a current revolving or other committed facility (keyword search of all seven sources); the only revolver found has a stated maturity of April 22, 2024 (S1 page:161). The liquidity chart carries Not supplied in every row.

- Adjusted EBITDA basis: FY2025 and FY2024 are on the earlier definition and no recast FY2025 figure is supplied; the LTM and the pro forma ratios inherit this. Remediation: obtain the recast FY2025 figure, or keep the sensitivity of 0.9 in C1.

- Pro forma interest: Not calculable. The Applicable Rate on the 850.0 first lien term loan is defined in a credit agreement that is not supplied (S4 page:36), and the Existing Exchangeable Notes toggle is not resolved for 2026. Only 303.5 of fixed coupon is calculable (C7).

- Pro forma cash: the net debt row deducts 32.7 of closing cash use only; the company says more fees will be paid from cash (S4 page:38), and the fourth-quarter loss on extinguishment of about 182.7 is an accounting estimate, not a cash figure.
- Covenant levels and headroom: Not supplied. No maintenance covenant level appears in the filings; executed debt documents are not supplied.

- Quarterly data for 2025: only the Q3 2025 and nine-month 2025 comparatives are printed in the 2026 reports; a discrete Q4 2025 quarter is not printed and would be FY2025 less 9M 2025 on mixed definitions.
- Cash held abroad: the split of 751.9 between U.S. markets (606.3) and International markets (145.6) is printed (S4 page:7), but transfer restrictions are not assessed.
- Group-level view: the Q3 2026 report has no Muvico Group or restricted-group presentation; the last such view is in the June 30, 2026 report (S3 page:67-73) and is not used here.
- Fiscal-year-end 2026 balance sheet and the effect of the refinancing on interest expense are after the cutoff and not in the sources.
## Next module

CP-1A should take the October 5, 2026 refinancing terms from the "Debt after the October 5, 2026 refinancing" table and the Note 11 chunks (S4 page:33-38), the repaid instruments from the debt register, and the equity issuance and exchange history for the transaction summary. CP-2 should read leverage as 4.50x on reported principal and trailing Adjusted EBITDA but carry the mixed-definition caveat, the absence of a described undrawn facility, the 3,761.9 of operating leases outside debt, the partial pro forma interest figure (303.5 of fixed coupons) and the unavailable covenant levels. CP-5 should trace each calculated figure to the printed inputs in the Calculations section and the locators above.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| AMC is a scaled, high-fixed-cost cinema operator whose results follow studio film supply. Earnings recovered in 2026 and the October 2026 refinancing extended maturities, but past structuring against existing lenders keeps monitoring needs high. | Medium | Ownership is not disclosed in the supplied sources, and the new financing documents are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Seven studio distributors supplied 83% of U.S. box office revenue in 2025. | Earnings and liquidity swing with a film slate the company cannot control. | High |
| Third quarter 2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin was 20.3% against 9.4% a year earlier on higher revenue. | Fixed rent and operating costs give operating leverage that works in both directions. | Medium |

| In July 2024 the company moved 175 theatres and intellectual property into unrestricted subsidiaries, then financed there. | Existing lenders' claims were separated from those assets; further liability management stays a monitoring point. | Medium |

| The October 5, 2026 refinancing raised 3,970.0 of new secured debt and repaid or discharged 3,666.5 of existing debt. | Maturities move to 2031 and later, but principal rises and a second lien layer ranks behind first lien debt. | High |
| Ownership is 99.75% in street name and the proxy-statement ownership table is not supplied. | Control, sponsor support and holder concentration cannot be assessed from the sources. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. is a listed, widely held theatre circuit with no sponsor identified in the supplied sources, and its creditor story is the interaction of an operating recovery with a history of active balance-sheet engineering. The operating base is large and geographically split: 855 theatres and 9,640 screens in 11 countries at December 31, 2025, and 840 theatres and 9,472 screens at September 30, 2026, with U.S. markets contributing 3,298.5 of 4,353.2 of nine-month 2026 revenue. Revenue is driven by attendance, which depends on a film slate controlled by a few studios, so revenue visibility is short and cash flow is seasonal. Against that, a largely fixed cost base (rent, operating expense and leases) gave strong operating leverage in 2026: third quarter revenue rose 31.6% and Adjusted EBITDA margin was 20.3% against 9.4%. The credit-relevant history is a sequence of transactions that moved debt and assets between entities: the July 2024 transfer of 175 theatres and intellectual property to unrestricted subsidiaries, the July 2025 exchange of part of the Existing 7.5% Notes into Muvico notes, repeated exchanges of debt for shares, and the October 5, 2026 refinancing that repaid the Muvico and Odeon term loans, the New 2029 Notes and most of the Existing 7.5% Notes with 2,000.0 of first lien notes, 850.0 of first lien term loans and 1,120.0 of second lien term loans. That refinancing is a subsequent event to the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and is kept separate from period facts below. Supportive actions are also documented, namely large equity issuance and note-for-share exchanges, but they were dilutive: shares outstanding rose from 512,943,561 at December 31, 2025 to 892,604,638 at September 30, 2026. Ownership concentration, sponsor behaviour beyond the issuer's own actions, and executed covenant terms cannot be read from the sources and remain open.
### Company and operating model
| Area | Fact | Category | Source | Creditor mechanism |

| Core activity and revenue model | Theatrical exhibition; revenues are "generated primarily from box office admissions and theatre food and beverage sales". Nine-month 2026 revenue was admissions 2,395.0, food and beverage 1,512.8 and other theatre 445.4, total 4,353.2 | Documentary Fact | S1 page:11; S4 page:2 | Revenue is transactional and recurs only through attendance, so there is no contracted revenue floor |

| Footprint | 855 theatres and 9,640 screens in 11 countries at December 31, 2025 (533 theatres and 7,072 screens in the United States; 322 and 2,568 in Europe); 840 theatres and 9,472 screens at September 30, 2026 | Documentary Fact | S1 page:9; S4 page:48 | Scale supports studio relationships; screen count is falling through closures: net closures of 43 screens in nine months 2026 |

| Segments | Two reportable segments, U.S. markets and International markets; international operations are attributed to Odeon and Nordic. Q3 2026 revenue was 1,299.1 U.S. and 412.0 International | Documentary Fact | S1 page:9; S4 page:27 | Cash flow is split across currencies (British pounds, euros, Swedish and Norwegian krone) while debt is in USD |

| Volume driver | Q3 2026 attendance 74.9 million against 58.4 million; nine months 193,829 thousand against 163,087 thousand. The company attributes the rise to "the popularity of film product" | Documentary Fact | S4 page:51; S4 page:48 | Volume depends on the film slate, so a weak release calendar lowers revenue with little offset |

| Pricing | Average ticket price rose 3.9% and food and beverage per patron rose 1.7% from $7.74 to $7.87 in Q3 2026 | Documentary Fact | S4 page:51 | Pricing and subscription mix add revenue per guest but cannot offset a volume shortfall alone |

| Film supply concentration | "seven movie studio distributors representing approximately 83% of our U.S. markets" box office revenues in 2025 and five representing about 76% of International | Documentary Fact | S1 page:41 | Supplier concentration gives studios bargaining power over film rental terms; film exhibition costs were 50.0% of admissions revenue in Q3 2026 against 49.3% |

| Release windows | The company states that the average exclusive theatrical window fell from "approximately four months to approximately one-and-one half months or less" | Documentary Fact | S1 page:41 | Shorter windows shift viewing to the home and lower the revenue per title |

| Cost structure | Food and beverage costs were 18.2% of food and beverage revenue against 19.6%; operating expense was 29.3% of revenues against 35.7%; rent was 221.2 in Q3 2026 against 224.1 | Documentary Fact | S4 page:52; S4 page:2 | A largely fixed base magnifies margin change in both directions |

| Operating leverage in results | Adjusted EBITDA margin 20.3% in Q3 2026 against 9.4%; revenue up 31.6% | Documentary Fact | S7 page:10; S4 page:51 | The same leverage would erode margin quickly if attendance fell |

| Lease commitments | Operating lease liabilities 3,761.9; cash paid for operating leases 704.7 in nine months 2026 | Documentary Fact | S4 page:9 | Fixed rent ranks alongside debt service and is not in the debt figure |

| Capital spending | Capital expenditures 158.8 in nine months 2026, split growth 64.9 and maintenance 90.5 before 3.4 of change in construction payables; 2026 net capital expenditure guidance "approximately $200.0 million to $235.0 million" | Documentary Fact (guidance is Management Language) | S7 page:14; S4 page:82 | Maintenance spending absorbs part of operating cash flow each year |

| Working capital | Admissions cash is received before film rentals are paid, 14 to 49 days later; deferred revenues were 452.6 | Documentary Fact | S4 page:79; S4 page:3 | The float funds operations but reverses after weak months |

| Loyalty and subscriptions | About 42.0 million member households; AMC Stubs members were about 52.0% of U.S. markets attendance in nine months 2026 | Documentary Fact | S4 page:44 | A recurring customer base supports attendance but does not guarantee volume |

| Advertising and NCM agreement | The amended exhibitor services agreement runs through February 13, 2042, with a financing discount rate of 16.12%; the liability is 454.3. Higher discount rates added 5.2 to advertising income in nine months 2026 | Documentary Fact | S4 page:47; S4 page:3; S4 page:63 | Part of other theatre revenue is recognised from the exhibitor services liability rather than from cash received in the period, which lifts Adjusted EBITDA relative to cash |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The transaction that matters most for creditors is the October 5, 2026 refinancing, which closed after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and is a subsequent event. S4 page:33 states that on that date "the Company completed a series of refinancing transactions", issuing 2,000.0 of 8.875% First Lien Notes due 2031 as issuer, borrowing 850.0 of first lien term loans under an amended and restated credit agreement, and borrowing 1,120.0 of second lien term loans from a lender identified as Deutsche Bank Special Situations Group (S4 page:34). The first lien term loans mature on October 5, 2031 with 0.25% quarterly amortization from March 31, 2027, and the second lien term loans mature on October 5, 2033 at a fixed 11.25% (S4 page:36). The 2031 Notes are secured on a first-priority basis, pari passu with the first lien term loans, by substantially all tangible and intangible assets of the company and the guarantors (S4 page:35). Intercreditor agreements separate three collateral groups: the AMC collateral, the Centertainment group and the Odeon group, and rank the Existing Exchangeable Notes first lien on the AMC collateral but second lien on the Centertainment collateral (S4 page:37). The proceeds repaid in full the Muvico Term Loans and the Odeon Term Loans, redeemed all 903.4 of the New 2029 Notes at 100.000% plus a make-whole premium of 144.3, accepted tenders for 355.5 of the 360.0 Existing 7.5% Notes and discharged the remainder for redemption on or about February 15, 2027 (S4 page:37-38). The company used about 32.7 of balance-sheet cash at closing and estimates a loss on extinguishment of about 182.7 in the fourth quarter of 2026 (S4 page:38). Taken from the CP-1 accepted figures, pro forma principal is 4,086.1 against 3,782.6 before, with 79.2% fixed rate, and the nearest large maturity moves from 2029 to 2031. The creditor mechanics are two: near-term refinancing risk falls, because the Muvico term loans, the Odeon term loans and the New 2029 Notes were the main 2029 and 2031 obligations; but senior secured claims are larger and a 1,120.0 second lien layer now sits behind 2,850.0 of new first lien debt, so recovery prospects for junior claims depend on collateral value that the sources do not quantify. This handoff states no expected recovery.

Earlier transactions explain why the structure is layered. On July 22, 2024 the company transferred the net assets of 175 theatres and 100% of certain intellectual property to Muvico through Centertainment, and Muvico licensed the intellectual property back to the operating subsidiary and engaged it under a management agreement to run the transferred theatres; Muvico and Centertainment (the Muvico Group) "are unrestricted subsidiaries under the indenture governing Holdings" for the purposes of the Existing 7.5% Notes (S1 page:100, S3 page:67). In the same month the company and Muvico jointly borrowed 2,024.3 of term loans and Muvico issued 414.4 of exchangeable notes to repurchase second lien notes (S1 page:156). In July 2025, under a transaction support agreement with "certain holders" of the Existing 7.5% Notes, Muvico issued 857.0 of New 2029 Notes for 590.0 of those notes plus 244.4 of new money (S1 page:95; S4 page:16), reducing the Existing 7.5% Notes from 950.0 at December 31, 2024 to 360.0 at December 31, 2025 (S1 page:142). The sources do not say whether every holder was offered the exchange. In 2026 the company paid consent fees in shares rather than cash, including 17,739,549 shares to holders of the New 2029 Notes for indenture amendments, exchanged all 155.8 of the New Exchangeable Notes for 142,102,295 shares with a loss on extinguishment of 33.0, refinanced the 400.0 Odeon Senior Secured Notes due 2027 with 425.0 of Odeon term loans that carried a Holdings guarantee, and raised equity (S4 page:14-18; S2 page:27). The 125.5 Senior Subordinated Notes due 2027 were redeemed on July 24, 2026 with proceeds of the June 2026 registered direct offering, within net equity issuance proceeds of 333.6 for nine months 2026 (S4 page:4, page:16, page:45). No dividends or shareholder distributions are printed in the nine-month cash flow statement (S4 page:4). Evidence quality for these transactions is High: they are filed, dated and issuer-specific, but executed indentures and credit agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity (what the documents permit) is inferred only from the filings' summaries.

spans.text: ## Request

This is the fundamental credit synthesis for AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway. It combines the accepted financial base and the business and transaction context, in USD, and gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources
This module reads the accepted upstream handoffs only and quotes no filing text. The filings and releases below are the issuer sources those handoffs rest on.
| Label | Exact source name | sha256 |
| S7 | EX-99.1_2026-11-04_amc-ex99d1.htm.jsonl | 51a7c35ada2d95a83a44b3a8c877a5584b3fe836e069b2ff43e63ad3815eecda |
Supplied handoffs:
| Module | sha256 | What this module takes from it |
| CP-0 | c885c49c340c71764325303325dd98265ae7aba265448e22f72e309753261f9e | Source readiness and the gap list |
| CP-1 | 8e7bd6a403005e8737f70ed50dbc8a7e41cbf01bba720956efc8b944b9480302 | Financial base: leverage, cover, liquidity, maturities, debt registers, claims outside debt |
| CP-1A | 3dc635c9d415eebd00632520a019d6eb70c35baba975237904827d7a7c9ba219 | Business model, transaction history, creditor-behaviour record, monitoring gaps |
Context file (settings only, not issuer evidence): sha256 0cce4dad135405f8586147db90660063f1faeb01eb8ee14c36784567b5aeaa09. It leaves ratings, quotes and valuation blank.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| AMC is a recovering but thinly cushioned credit: trailing earnings cut leverage to 4.50x and extended maturities, yet fixed charges, film-slate dependence and cash-only liquidity leave little room for a weak year. | Medium | Trailing earnings mix two definitions, covenant levels and executed documents are not supplied, and ownership is not disclosed. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 840.4 million cut total debt leverage to 4.50x from 10.39x at FY2025. | Debt service capacity improved materially, but the trailing figure mixes two Adjusted EBITDA definitions. | Medium |
| Fixed-charge cover, counting rent and cash interest, is about 1.35x on trailing earnings. | Little room remains if attendance weakens, because rent ranks alongside debt service. | Medium |
| Cash of USD 751.9 million is the only stated source of liquidity; no committed facility is described. | Liquidity has no backstop beyond cash and operating cash flow. | Medium |

| The October 2026 refinancing moved the main maturities to 2031 and 2033 but raised principal to USD 4,086.1 million. | Near-term refinancing risk is lower; leverage is 4.86x pro forma and a second lien layer is added. | High |
| Earnings follow a film slate controlled by seven distributors that supplied 83% of U.S. box office revenue. | A weak slate hits revenue, margin and cash flow at once. | High |
### Credit view

AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. is a recovering but thinly cushioned credit: earnings have rebounded sharply, yet its fixed charges leave little margin if film attendance weakens. The strongest support is trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 840.4 million, which brings total debt to 4.50x, cash interest cover to 2.14x and free cash flow to USD 168.0 million, while cash of USD 751.9 million and the October 2026 refinancing push the main maturities to 2031 and 2033. The weakest point is that liquidity is cash alone, with no committed facility described, and fixed-charge cover including rent is only about 1.35x. What decides the outcome is whether attendance and the studio film slate hold near 2026 levels.
### Credit assessment
| Item | View | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Improving, still high-risk: leverage and cash interest cover improved sharply on trailing earnings, but cover after rent is thin, liquidity is cash only and results depend on film supply | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Financial base: leverage, interest cover, liquidity, claims outside debt; business context: film supply, operating leverage |

| Thesis | AMC has used a strong 2026 box office to cut leverage and extend maturities, but it carries fixed rent and a larger secured debt stack that only sustained attendance can service | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | As above, with the October 2026 refinancing |

| Limit on confidence | Below High because the business context was judged ready with limitations for this synthesis, and ownership, executed documents, covenant levels and an undrawn facility are not evidenced | Insufficient Information | Not applicable | Readiness handoff gaps; business context monitoring gaps |
### Key findings

Deleveraging is real but earnings-led. AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. reports principal debt of USD 3,782.6 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 4,024.2 million at December 31, 2025, while trailing Adjusted EBITDA is USD 840.4 million against USD 387.5 million for FY2025. Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is therefore 4.50x, down from 10.39x, and 3.61x net of USD 751.9 million of cash. Most of the improvement comes from the earnings side, which means leverage will move back up quickly if earnings fall (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). The trailing figure combines FY2025 on the earlier Adjusted EBITDA definition with 2026 on the revised one, a difference worth about USD 0.9 million on the nine-month comparison and unquantified for FY2025.

Cash interest cover is adequate on trailing earnings but was below 1.0x a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.14x over the twelve months to September 30, 2026, against 0.95x in FY2025 and 0.86x in FY2024. A cover that moved from below to above 1.0x between FY2025 and the twelve months to September 30, 2026 shows how exposed debt service is to the earnings level.

Fixed charges beyond debt are the main cushion issue. Operating lease liabilities of USD 3,761.9 million sit outside reported debt, and cash paid for operating leases was USD 704.7 million in nine months 2026. Adjusted EBITDA plus rent covered cash interest plus rent about 1.35x on trailing figures against 0.99x in FY2025 (Analyst Interpretation from the financial base). Rent does not flex with attendance, so the cushion falls quickly in a weak year.

Liquidity is cash, and cash is the only stated backstop. Cash was USD 751.9 million at September 30, 2026, up from USD 428.5 million at December 31, 2025, and no committed undrawn facility is described. Operating cash flow is seasonal: USD 128.5 million was used in the first quarter of 2026, then USD 235.4 million and USD 176.6 million were provided in the second and third. Free cash flow is USD 168.0 million over the trailing twelve months after USD 365.9 million of negative free cash flow in FY2025.

The October 2026 refinancing removes near-term maturities but adds debt. Pro forma principal after October 5, 2026 is USD 4,086.1 million, with USD 8.5 million a year of amortization before 2030, USD 2,816.0 million due in 2031 and USD 1,120.0 million of second lien term loans due in 2033; 79.2% is fixed rate. Pro forma total debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA is 4.86x. The fixed coupons on the new notes and second lien term loans alone are USD 303.5 million a year, and the floating margin on USD 850.0 million of first lien term loans is not printed, so pro forma interest cover cannot be computed from the sources.

Business risk is concentrated in supply and operating leverage. Seven distributors supplied about 83% of U.S. box office revenue in 2025, release windows have shortened, and attendance in the third quarter of 2026 rose from 58.4 million to 74.9 million on film popularity (Documentary Fact). The Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 9.4% to 20.3% on 31.6% higher revenue, the operating leverage that also works against creditors in a weak slate.

The record of dealing with lenders raises the monitoring bar. AMC moved 175 theatres and intellectual property into unrestricted subsidiaries in July 2024, financed there, exchanged USD 590.0 million of USD 950.0 million of the Existing 7.5% Notes into Muvico notes in 2025 with certain holders, and has repeatedly paid consent fees and exchanged debt in shares, lifting shares outstanding from 512,943,561 to 892,604,638 during 2026 (Documentary Fact; the creditor-adverse reading is Analyst Interpretation). It also repaid the Muvico and Odeon term loans in full in October 2026, which removes those structures from the debt stack.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Scale and footprint: AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. operated 840 theatres and 9,472 screens at September 30, 2026 across the United States and Europe, with about 42.0 million loyalty member households, which gives it purchasing weight with studios and a recurring customer base (Documentary Fact; the market-leader claim is Management Language and is not adopted). Operating recovery: trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 840.4 million is more than double FY2025, and free cash flow turned positive at USD 168.0 million (Documentary Fact). Maturity profile: the October 2026 refinancing leaves only USD 8.5 million a year of principal before 2030 and pushes USD 2,816.0 million to 2031 (Documentary Fact). Access to capital: AMC raised USD 333.6 million of net equity proceeds in nine months 2026 and raised USD 3,970.0 million of new debt on one day, showing market access for now (Documentary Fact; the durability of that access is Analyst Interpretation). Cash: USD 751.9 million is held, USD 145.6 million of it by the International markets operations, whose availability to the group was not assessed (Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. Film supply dependence: seven distributors supplied about 83% of U.S. box office revenue and windows have shortened, so revenue visibility is short (Documentary Fact). Thin fixed-charge cover: cover including rent is about 1.35x on trailing figures and was 0.99x in FY2025, and USD 3,761.9 million of operating lease liabilities sit outside debt (Analyst Interpretation from the financial base). No described backstop liquidity: no committed undrawn facility is described, so a weak slate would draw directly on cash (Insufficient Information on whether one exists; the missing datapoint is the executed credit agreements). Higher debt: pro forma principal rises to USD 4,086.1 million, with USD 1,120.0 million of second lien debt behind USD 2,850.0 million of new first lien debt, so junior claims depend on collateral values the sources do not quantify (Documentary Fact; recovery is not assessed here). Creditor-behaviour record and dilution: the unrestricted subsidiary transfer, partial exchanges and share-paid fees show a willingness to restructure around existing lenders, and about 143,258,701 authorized shares remain unissued and unreserved, limiting further equity-funded exchanges (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Information limits: ownership, covenant levels and executed financing documents are not supplied (Insufficient Information).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |
| Weak film slate or shorter windows | Attendance falls while rent and operating costs stay largely fixed | Margin and cash flow fall faster than revenue; cover after rent is about 1.35x | Material |
| Liquidity with no described facility | Cash is the only backstop and operating cash flow is seasonal | A weak quarter draws directly on USD 751.9 million of cash | Material |

| Higher secured debt after October 5, 2026 | Principal rises to USD 4,086.1 million with a second lien layer and fixed coupons of USD 303.5 million | Debt service steps up; refinancing risk moves out to 2031 and 2033 | Material |

| Further liability management | History of unrestricted subsidiary transfer, partial exchanges and share-paid fees | Existing lenders' position may change again; monitor new designations and amendments | Material |

| Definition and basis risk | Trailing Adjusted EBITDA mixes definitions; add-backs include stock-based compensation and other expense | Leverage may be understated or overstated by an unquantified amount | Minor |
| Dilution and equity capacity | Share count up sharply; limited authorized headroom | Equity-funded repayments may be harder to repeat | Minor |
## Calculations
All inputs are figures in the accepted financial base, in USD millions.
C1. Fixed-charge cover, an analyst measure the issuer does not define: (Adjusted EBITDA + rent expense) / (cash interest paid + rent expense), where rent is the statement-of-operations rent line.

C2. Free cash flow buffer: trailing free cash flow of 168.0 as a share of trailing Adjusted EBITDA of 840.4 is 20.0%. A fall in Adjusted EBITDA of 168.0, with every other item unchanged including working capital, would take trailing free cash flow to zero. This is arithmetic, not a forecast.

C3. Cash interest break-even: trailing Adjusted EBITDA could fall by 840.4 - 392.3 = 448.1, or 53.3%, before cash interest cover reaches 1.0x; this ignores capital expenditure of 242.2, which free cash flow in C2 does include.

C4. Pro forma fixed obligations from the financial base: stated coupons of 303.5 plus first lien term loan amortization of 8.5 give 312.0 a year of the debt service that can be computed; the floating margin on 850.0 and the toggle on the Existing Exchangeable Notes are not printed.
C5. Pro forma first lien debt: 2,000.0 of 2031 Notes + 850.0 of first lien term loans = 2,850.0; second lien 1,120.0.

C6. Directions used in the text: leverage fell from 10.39x to 4.50x (financial base, calculated); cash rose from 428.5 to 751.9; cash interest cover rose from 0.95x to 2.14x; shares outstanding rose from 512,943,561 to 892,604,638 (business context).
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | What it affects | Severity | Action |

| Executed indentures and credit agreements, including covenant levels, are not supplied | Priming, guarantee, collateral release and unrestricted subsidiary terms and any covenant headroom cannot be read | Covenant view, recovery mechanics, legal-rights statements | Material | Add the October 6, 2026 Form 8-K exhibits |

| No committed undrawn facility is described; absence is not a printed zero | Liquidity may be understated if a facility exists | Liquidity view and the liquidity chart | Material | Confirm in the executed credit agreements |
| Trailing Adjusted EBITDA mixes definitions; FY2025 is not recast | Leverage and cover may shift by an unquantified amount | All trailing ratios | Minor | Obtain recast FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA |

| Pro forma interest cannot be computed: first lien margin and Exchangeable Notes toggle are not printed | Post-refinancing cover is unknown | Pro forma interest cover | Material | Obtain the credit agreement margin |
| Ownership and sponsor behaviour beyond issuer actions are not supplied | Control and support cannot be assessed | Governance view | Minor | Add the annual meeting proxy statement |

| Terms of the 2025 exchange offer, including whether all holders were offered it, are not supplied | The creditor-adverse reading of that exchange is conditional | Creditor-behaviour assessment | Minor | Obtain the 2025 transaction documents |
| Business context judged this synthesis ready with limitations rather than ready | Confidence is held below High | The overall assessment | Minor | Resolve the gaps above |
## Next module

CP-5 should trace each figure in this synthesis to the accepted financial base and business context and confirm that the two fixed-charge and free cash flow calculations rest on printed inputs. The key findings and strengths and weaknesses are the report sections this module feeds.
